Immanuel Kant on enlightenment

Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) approaches enlightenment within German idealism. He argued that experience is structured by a priori forms and categories, and that morality rests on autonomy and the categorical imperative. Systematically, the teaching links epistemology, ethics, aesthetics, law into a practical and theoretical whole. On this page, the archive isolates English passages where that project meets enlightenment most directly—useful for searches such as “immanuel kant quotes on enlightenment.”

How to use this page

Start with the shortest passage, then compare tone across sources. Return to the Immanuel Kant thinker page for biography and to the enlightenment theme for other voices on the same question.
